meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at a run / quickly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я сам их встречу, бегом наверх!
examples.trans: I will meet them myself, run upstairs!
No time to explain, run faster!

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'without' in everyday speech.
слава богу = thank God (literally 'glory to God')

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!

future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'yesterday' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.

examples.trans: Hold on! Two days is far too little.

Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Что у кого. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'обрать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away (by force), confiscate', paired with 'отбирать'.

examples.trans: Oh sure, right now they'll take them away!

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, послушайте. Будете лезть не в своё дело, телевизоры отберём!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, listen. If you meddle in what's not your business, we'll take the TVs away!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'правлять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you are sending'.

examples.text: Дима, а почему ты меня домой отправляешь?
examples.trans: Dima, why are you sending me home?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и отправлять вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and you are sending on time.

related.gloss: not to you are sending (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Locative / directional adverb. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'говорщик'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'negotiator' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть переговорщик.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always negotiator.

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'дукт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'product, foodstuff' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты будешь целый день разгружать продукты!
examples.trans: You will unload groceries the whole day!
The guests need the freshest product!

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Spoken exchange. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'conversation, talk' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас с тобой серьёзный разговор.
examples.trans: You and I have a serious talk to have.

examples.text: Есть интересный разговор. Всё хорошо, малыш.
examples.trans: There's an interesting conversation. Everything is fine, kid.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!
Colloquial plural of ребёнок. Common substantive noun meaning 'guys, lads, kids (plural only)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.

meanings.note: colloquial: нет света = the power is off
colloquial: нет света = the power is off
В целом свете = in the whole world. Common masculine noun meaning 'light; electricity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тереть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you will erase / delete'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и стереть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and you will erase on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют стереть.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to you will erase.

related.gloss: not to you will erase (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Also a mobile phone. International compound from Greek 'tele' (far) + 'phone' (voice, sound).

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.en: to make it, to be in time
meanings.note: + на: успеть на поезд = catch the train

+ infinitive. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make it, to be in time', paired with 'успевать'.

examples.trans: We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.
